newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares fall pre-bourse on French left win.
newsitem.headline: German shares fall pre-bourse on French left win.

text.p: German shares were lower in pre-bourse trade on Monday, but more stable than many commentators had expected, after an upset victory for the French left in Sunday's election hit sentiment.
By 0736 GMT the IBIS DAX index was down 14.17 points, or 0.40 percent, at 3,548.53 points, with support coming from a stronger dollar at 1.7120/30 marks.

"There is a lot of uncertainty about, what with the gold reserves revaluation being debated back and forth and the uncertainty after the French elections. It doesn't add to confidence at the start of the week," a Frankfurt broker said.

"There are numbers coming out of the U.S. this week as well, so you might have people sitting on the sidelines waiting for those," the broker said, referring to NAPM figures today and factory orders figures on Wednesday. "This is not a crash day, but we're not going up anywhere," he said.
A trader was more pessimistic. "The market hasn't really gone down yet, but it will," he said.

The biggest losers in early IBIS electronic trade were sportswear groups Puma AG and Adidas AG. The sportswear sector fell out of favour late last week when the U.S. giant Nike issued a profit warning.
Puma was down 1.40 marks, or 2.60 percent, at 52.50 marks, while Adidas was down two marks, or 1.10 percent, 179 marks.
The strength of the dollar boosted exporters, including the carmakers. Volkswagen was up eight marks at 1,113 marks, while BMW was up five marks at 1,395 marks.
